arguments.content:
# Boolean settings

`parse_bool(value, default=False)` reads an environment-style boolean setting.

## Accepted tokens

- True: `true`, `1`, `yes`, `on`
- False: `false`, `0`, `no`, `off`

Matching ignores case and surrounding whitespace, so `" \tYeS\n"` is `True` and `"OFF"` is `False`.

## Defaults

`None`, empty strings, and whitespace-only strings return the supplied `default` (a bool, `False` unless overridden). An explicit token always wins over the default.

## Invalid values

Any other string raises `ValueError`; a nonempty string is not automatically true.

## Examples

- `parse_bool("OFF") -> False`
- `parse_bool("", default=True) -> True`

## Verify

Run the test suite with:

```
python3 -B -S -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```
